subject: atomic vector error when using gl.outflank

messages.author: dee4a1d9a9f05256
messages.subject: atomic vector error when using gl.outflank
parts:
Hi,

I'm attempting to run outlier detection with gl.outflank. I ran it successfully on a gl object, but then needed to update my populations. After updating the populations (code below), the function returns the following error: Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

The function still works with the old populations, but not with the new ones.

Any insight would be much appreciated! Let me know if you need more information and thanks in advance!

MR.vcf=read.vcfR('MigRes_fullpheno_populations.snps.vcf')
MR.vcf
# ***** Object of Class vcfR *****
#   100 samples
# 2547 CHROMs
# 4,201 variants
# Object size: 26.1 Mb
# 6.966 percent missing data
# *****        *****         *****

#convert to genlight
MR.gl=vcfR2genlight(MR.vcf)
MR.gl

#add new populations
all(colnames(MR.gl)[-1] == popmap2$STRATA)
pop(MR.gl)= popmap2$STRATA

AFU2.out = gl.outflank(MR.gl, plot = TRUE, LeftTrimFraction = 0.05,
                      RightTrimFraction = 0.05, Hmin = 0.1, qthreshold = 0.05)
Start conversion....
Please note conversion of bigger data sets will take some time!
Once finished, we recommend to save the object using >save(object, file="object.rdata")
  |================================================================================================================================| 100%
Matrix converted.. Prepare genind object...

Finished! Took 2 seconds.
Calculating FSTs, may take a few minutes...
All loci with Fst above the upper (righthand) trim point were marked as outliers. Re-run with smaller RightTrimFraction or smaller qthreshold.
Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors


> is.atomic(MR.gl)
[1] FALSE

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] atomic vector error when using gl.outflank
parts:
Hi Justine,

When you step outside the dartR scripts, the risk is that all the small things we track get missed. To capture this, run

gl <- gl.compliance.check(gl)

and try again.

A
